cards.front: Distinguish between system software and application software.
cards.back: System software runs and manages the computer itself, providing a platform for other programs, such as an operating system, a driver or a utility. Application software carries out tasks for the user, such as a spreadsheet or a game.

keyPoints.text: system software manages the computer and provides a platform
application software performs tasks for the user
an example of each

mcq.correct: System software runs and manages the computer itself, providing a platform for other programs, such as an operating system, a driver or a utility. Application software carries out tasks for the user, such as a spreadsheet or a game.
distractors: System software is written by the user and application software by the manufacturer
System software is always stored in ROM and application software in RAM
Application software manages hardware while system software performs user tasks

cards.explanation: The distinction is about purpose, not about who wrote it or where it is stored: both kinds can be installed and updated.

cards.front: What is meant by the operating system acting as a resource manager?
cards.back: It allocates the processor, memory, storage and peripherals between competing programs, deciding which program runs when and how much of each resource it gets.

keyPoints.text: allocates processor time
allocates memory
manages peripherals or storage

cards.explanation: Without arbitration, two programs could write to the same memory or send output to the same device at the same time.

cards.front: Define a software library and give one advantage of using one.
cards.back: A collection of pre-written, tested routines that a program can call rather than implement itself. An advantage is that less code has to be written and debugged, and the routines are reusable across programs.

keyPoints.text: pre-written reusable routines or classes
synonyms: a collection of code that can be called

keyPoints.text: less code to write and test

cards.explanation: A library is linked in at translation time, unlike a web API which is called over a network at run time.

cards.front: How does open-source software differ from proprietary software?
cards.back: Open-source software makes its source code available to read, modify and redistribute, usually under a licence that sets the terms. Proprietary software is distributed in compiled form with the source kept secret and copying or modification restricted.

keyPoints.text: source code is available to inspect and modify
can be redistributed
proprietary software keeps the source secret

cards.explanation: Free of charge and open source are different things: open source is about the licence and the source code, not the price.

cards.front: Give three functions performed by an operating system.
cards.back: Any three of: memory management, process scheduling, file and disk management, device management through drivers, providing a user interface, and managing security and access rights.

keyPoints.text: memory management
process scheduling
file or disk management
device management
security and access rights

cards.explanation: Three of these are enough for full credit; the point is that they are all things no application can be trusted to do for itself.

cards.front: Name three kinds of utility software and say what each does.
cards.back: For example: a disk defragmenter, which reorganises files into contiguous blocks; an antivirus scanner, which detects and removes malware; and a backup tool, which copies data for recovery.

keyPoints.text: disk defragmentation
antivirus or malware protection
backup or file compression

distractors: Word processor, spreadsheet, database
Compiler, interpreter, assembler
Operating system, device driver, firmware

cards.explanation: Utilities support and maintain the computer rather than doing user work, which is what separates them from application software - the second option is a list of applications. They sit close to system software, and the boundary is genuinely fuzzy: an antivirus package is bought like an application but performs a system maintenance role.

cards.front: How does virtual memory allow a computer to run programs larger than its physical RAM?
cards.back: Parts of a program not currently in use are moved to disk, and the memory manager swaps pages back in when they are needed, so the address space can exceed the physical memory.

keyPoints.text: unused pages are moved to disk
pages are brought back when needed
the address space can exceed physical RAM

mcq.correct: Unused pages go to disk and are swapped back in on demand
distractors: The program is compressed so it fits in RAM
Extra RAM is allocated from the processor cache
The program is split and run in pieces on different cores

cards.explanation: The cost is speed: a page fault means a disk access, which is orders of magnitude slower than RAM. When too many processes compete for too little memory the system spends most of its time swapping rather than working, which is thrashing. Virtual memory also gives each process its own address space, so one program cannot corrupt another's memory.

cards.front: Describe round robin scheduling and state one disadvantage.
cards.back: Each process is given a fixed time slice in turn, and one that has not finished goes to the back of the queue. A disadvantage is that a short time slice wastes time in context switching, while a long one gives poor response.

keyPoints.text: each process gets a fixed time slice
an unfinished process goes to the back of the queue
too short a slice wastes time switching
synonyms: too long a slice gives poor response

mcq.correct: Fixed time slices in turn; switching overhead if the slice is too short
distractors: Longest job first; short jobs may never run
Highest priority always; equal-priority jobs starve
First come first served; a long job blocks everything

cards.explanation: Round robin is fair and gives predictable response, which suits time-sharing systems. The tuning problem is real: a 1 ms slice on a system where a context switch takes 0.2 ms spends a fifth of its time switching. The other options are genuine alternative schedulers, each with the disadvantage named beside it.

cards.front: What is a device driver, and why is it needed?
cards.back: Software that lets the operating system communicate with a particular piece of hardware, translating the OS's general commands into the signals that device understands.

keyPoints.text: it lets the OS talk to specific hardware
synonyms: translates OS commands to the device

keyPoints.text: each device needs its own driver
the OS does not need to know the details of every device

mcq.correct: Software translating OS commands into signals a specific device understands
distractors: A physical component inside the device
A program that makes the device run faster
The cable connecting the device to the computer

cards.explanation: Drivers are the layer that keeps the operating system independent of the hardware: the OS issues a general 'print this' command and the printer's driver turns it into the codes that printer accepts. This is why installing new hardware usually means installing a driver, and why an operating system upgrade can break devices whose drivers were not updated.

cards.front: Where does firmware fit between hardware and software? Give an example.
cards.back: Firmware is software stored permanently in read-only memory on the device itself, so it behaves like hardware but can sometimes be updated. The BIOS or UEFI on a motherboard is the standard example.

keyPoints.text: software held permanently on the device
it can sometimes be updated
BIOS or UEFI is the standard example

mcq.correct: Permanent software in ROM on the device, such as BIOS or UEFI
distractors: Software installed on the hard disk by the manufacturer
Hardware that cannot ever be changed
Application software supplied with the device

cards.explanation: Firmware is what runs before there is an operating system - the BIOS or UEFI performs the power-on self test and then loads the bootloader. Router firmware is a more familiar example of the updatable kind, and the security risk of unpatched firmware is precisely that it sits below the operating system where ordinary updates cannot reach it.

cards.front: Give three advantages of using a software library rather than writing the code yourself.
cards.back: The code is already written and tested, so development is faster; it is likely to be well tested and free of common errors; and maintenance is handled by others, so bug fixes and improvements arrive without extra effort.

keyPoints.text: development is faster
it is tested and reliable
maintenance and updates are handled by others

mcq.correct: Faster development, proven reliability, and maintenance by others
distractors: Smaller files, faster execution and no documentation needed
No testing needed, no licensing and full control of the code
It always runs faster than hand-written code

cards.explanation: The trade-offs are worth naming as well: a library adds a dependency, may be larger than needed, and its licence may restrict commercial use. A security fault in a widely used library affects every program that includes it, which is what happened in several high-profile supply-chain incidents.

cards.front: How do the freedoms granted by an open-source licence differ from the restrictions of a proprietary EULA?
cards.back: An open-source licence grants the right to read, modify and redistribute the source code, usually on condition that changes are shared under the same terms. A proprietary EULA grants only the right to run the program, and normally forbids copying, modifying and reverse engineering.

keyPoints.text: open source allows the source to be read and modified
open source allows redistribution
a proprietary EULA grants only the right to run the software
a EULA normally forbids copying and reverse engineering

mcq.correct: Open source: read, modify, redistribute. EULA: run only, no copying or modification
distractors: Open source: free of charge. EULA: paid
Open source: no support. EULA: full support
Both allow modification, but only one allows copying

cards.explanation: The distinction is about rights, not price: open-source software can be sold and proprietary software can be given away free. Note that 'free to use' is not the same as open source - freeware usually ships without its source, so none of the four freedoms apply. Copyleft licences such as the GPL add the condition that derivative works stay under the same licence.
